extracted.intended_audience: YouTube creators, social media managers, digital marketers, and influencers seeking to increase organic reach and views
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, platform-specific guidance for making YouTube content (both long-form and Shorts) more likely to be recommended by the 2025 YouTube algorithm, including ranking factors, format-specific rules, and tactical tips for titles, thumbnails, retention, accessibility, and analytics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall ranking factors (engagement, user behavior, long-term relevance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendation system ranks content based on a mix of engagement, user behavior, and long-term relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factors work together to determine which videos show up in search results, home feeds, and suggested videos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewer engagement signals
rubrics_metrics.description: Traditional ranking factors that help YouTube assess whether a video is worth recommending: click-through rate (CTR); watch time & retention; likes, comments, and shares; negative feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How to boost: improve thumbnails and titles to increase CTR; deliver value quickly to improve retention. Negative feedback (e.g., 'Not Interested', dislikes) can suppress recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-through rate (CTR)
rubrics_metrics.description: How often users click on your video when they see it in search results or recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Improve CTR with clickable (but not misleading) titles and compelling thumbnails. Keep titles under 60 characters to avoid truncation. Test thumbnails and titles to find what increases CTR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watch time and retention
rubrics_metrics.description: Total minutes watched and the average percentage of the video viewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YouTube favors videos that keep viewers watching; focus on hooks, pacing, and content that maintains attention. Use audience retention metrics to identify drop-off points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likes, comments, and shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct engagement signals indicating interest from viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage interaction via CTAs, questions, polls, and pinned comments; more engagement signals can improve recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions like 'Not Interested' or dislikes that indicate viewers don't want the content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High negative feedback will reduce recommendations — avoid misleading titles/thumbnails and poor viewer experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewer satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures of whether viewers had a positive experience, beyond just time spent watching, including satisfaction surveys, post-watch behavior, replays & return viewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YouTube collects surveys to gauge satisfaction. Prioritize hooks and value, avoid unnecessary intros, and create content that prompts rewatching or return visits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-watch behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the viewer continues watching more content on YouTube or leaves the platform after a video.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Videos that keep viewers on the platform (drive further viewing) signal higher satisfaction and are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalized recommendations (user behavior & context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are customized per user using watch history, viewing habits, device type, and time of day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should be designed with session context in mind (e.g., short-form vs. long-form suited to mobile morning vs. TV night). Use playlists and end screens to encourage session continuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-term relevance (evergreen vs. trending)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube resurfaces older content when it becomes relevant due to search trends, nostalgia, or seasonal cycles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize older videos by updating thumbnails, descriptions, and pinned comments when trends spike. Target seasonal interest (e.g., fitness in January).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-language and global audience optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos with multi-language support (dubbing, translated metadata, captions) reach more regions and may perform better globally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: YouTube tracks performance per language; prioritize dubbing/translating best-performing content first. Localize titles/descriptions/subtitles and consider dubbing at-scale (channels that dub ~80% of catalog tend to perform better).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation surface differences (Home, Suggested, Search)
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube combines ranking factors differently depending on where recommendations appear: Home feed, Suggested videos alongside a current video, and personalized Search results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home uses performance metrics and user history; Suggested videos factor the current video's topic and watch history; Search mixes relevance of title/description/content with performance metrics. Optimize metadata and video performance according to the intended surface.

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube Shorts algorithm: testing and gradual scaling
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorts are tested with small audiences first; if they perform well they are recommended to wider audiences, and can go viral weeks or months after posting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload timing/quantity are not crucial; focus on quality. Give Shorts time to be tested across audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: YouTube Shorts ranking factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Shorts are ranked primarily on engagement, watch duration (percentage of Short watched), replays/loops, content variety, and user preferences; CTR is not a ranking factor for Shorts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for high watch duration (e.g., a 30s Short with 85% watch duration can outrank a 60s Short with 50% retention). Encourage loops/rewatches and use trending audio/effects. Avoid showing many Shorts from same creator back-to-back.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: view duration importance (not total watch time)
rubrics_metrics.description: View duration (percentage of the Short watched) matters much more than total watch time for Shorts ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shorts that achieve high percentage completion and natural looping are favored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts: CTR is not a ranking factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike long-form videos, CTR isn't considered for Shorts because users swipe through content rather than clicking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on first-frame hooks and watch duration instead of click-driven tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shorts monetization rules and funneling
rubrics_metrics.description: Watch time from Shorts does not count toward long-form monetization, but Shorts can qualify for Shorts Ad Revenue Sharing; subscribers gained via Shorts count toward monetization eligibility; Shorts that drive long-form views help channel growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Shorts to funnel viewers to longer videos via pinned comments, CTAs, and playlists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keyword research and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube is a search engine; use accurate, concise language people already search for and place primary keywords in file name, title, description (first two lines), and subtitles/captions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not overuse tags — tags play a minimal role except for misspellings. Avoid keyword stuffing (it's against YouTube policies on spam/deceptive practices). Use tools like Google Keyword Planner and YouTube search suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Titles: clickable but not clickbaity
rubrics_metrics.description: Create titles that drive CTR (curiosity-driven, numbers/lists) while avoiding misleading language that triggers quick bounce/negative feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use curiosity-driven phrases and lists, keep under 60 characters, and ensure title delivers on the promise to avoid suppression by the algorithm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thumbnails: custom, consistent, and high-impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Custom thumbnails that use a consistent style, high-contrast colors, bold text, and expressive faces/action shots improve CTR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep visual style consistent across thumbnails. Tools like Canva can help. Test thumbnails and iterate; update thumbnails and track CTR improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending topics and timely content
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube boosts fresh content related to current events, trends, and viral topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Google Trends or YouTube Trending to spot opportunities; only pursue trends that align with your niche and brand voice. Jump on seasonal/recurring topics when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attracting views from external sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Views from off-site (ads, embeds, social cross-promotion) are acceptable and can inform video success, though context matters for how the algorithm interprets performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External traffic won't be punished, but metrics may behave differently (CTR/retention changes). Embedding videos on blogs helps both site SEO and video view counts. Algorithm focuses on context — performance on a given surface influences further distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage comments, shares, and saves
rubrics_metrics.description: Fostering direct engagement signals (comments, shares, saves) helps grow audience and signals to YouTube that a video is worth recommending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask direct questions, use polls & pinned comments, and end with clear CTAs to encourage interaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to comments and community engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: Active creator interaction (replying to early comments, using the heart, pinning great comments) can boost ranking in early hours and sustain conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply to early comments to boost initial engagement, pin valuable comments, and use moderation tools (held for review) to manage spam.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post when your audience is online (use scheduling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although posting time isn't a direct ranking signal, publishing when your audience is online maximizes initial views and engagement, which influence algorithmic distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prep videos in advance and use scheduling tools (e.g., Hootsuite) to post at recommended times for your audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility (captions, alt text, descriptive captions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Design content to be inclusive: closed captioning, alt text for thumbnails, and descriptive captions improve accessibility and broaden reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ignoring accessibility excludes many viewers and reduces engagement; provide SRT files, readable captions, and thumbnail alt text to help discoverability and accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook viewers in the first few seconds
rubrics_metrics.description: Capture attention immediately (within the first ~2–5 seconds) because early drop-off harms recommendation prospects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cut slow intros, use teasers ('By the end of this video you’ll know…'), and add fast cuts/graphics/on-screen text to retain interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use chapters and timestamps
rubrics_metrics.description: Well-structured longer videos benefit from chapters/timestamps allowing viewers to jump to sections and preview content, which can improve CTR and retention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add timestamps in the description (e.g., '0:00 Intro | 1:30 Step 1 | 3:45 Final Tips'). Chapters also help preview content in search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create binge-worthy playlists
rubrics_metrics.description: Thematic playlists increase session watch time, a top algorithmic signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group videos into thematic playlists and enable autoplay next video to keep viewers within your channel ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use end screens and cards
rubrics_metrics.description: End screens and cards guide viewers to more content and increase retention by promoting related videos, playists, or subscribe actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add 2–3 end screen elements (next video, subscribe, playlist) and use cards during videos to recommend related content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze analytics regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Data and analytics are essential: study YouTube analytics (or third-party tools) to understand audience demographics, engagement, watch time, and behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use insights to report to teams and iterate strategy. Dig into location, gender, age and retention metrics to inform content decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test and iterate (video length, thumbnails, titles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Experimentation is key: test lengths, thumbnails, and title styles because YouTube favors engagement over length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience retention to determine preferred lengths; change thumbnails and monitor CTR improvements; try different title formats (question-based, list-based) and measure results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitor benchmarking
rubrics_metrics.description: Study top competitors to identify what they do better or worse (thumbnails, descriptions, cross-promotion) and adapt successful tactics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If competitors outperform you, analyze their approach; if you outperform them, document what's working and scale it.
